t: For research, surveys, training, dissemination of information, and demonstrations in education and in librarianship as authorized by the Act of July 26, 1954 (20 U.S.C. 331–332(b)), as amended by title IV of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965, and the Elementary and Secondary Education Amendments of 1966; section 4(c) of the Vocational Education Act of 1963 (20 U.S.C. 35C(c)); section 224 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (Public Law 89–329); and section 602 and title VII of the National Defense Education Act of 1958 as amended (20 U.S.C. ch. 17; Public Law 88–665), $90,967,000 of which $1,250,000 shall be available for program evaluation without regard to the provision in subsection 2(a)(2) of said Act of July 26, 1954, as amended, and $13,550,000 shall be available for research and special project activities under section 4(c) of said Vocational Education Act of 1963.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision that funds education and librarianship research, surveys, training, dissemination of information, and demonstrations under existing statutes. The tempting reading is that "dissemination of information" or "demonstrations" imply public involvement, but these are funded program activities, not a process in which outside parties are consulted before a federal decision. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: $90,967,000 of which $1,250,000 shall be available for program evaluation

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes funding for specific activities such as research, surveys, and training. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The text merely lists authorized activities and allocates funds, without mentioning advisory boards, public hearings, comment periods, or consultation requirements with non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: For research, surveys, training, dissemination of information, and demonstrations in education and in librarianship as authorized by the Act of July 26, 1954 (20 U.S.C. 331–332(b)), as amended by title IV of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965, and the Elementary and Secondary Education Amendments of 1966; section 4(c) of the Vocational Education Act of 1963 (20 U.S.C. 35C(c)); section 224 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (Public Law 89–329); and section 602 and title VII of the National Defense Education Act of 1958 as amended (20 U.S.C. ch. 17; Public Law 88–665), $90,967,000 of which $1,250,000 shall be available for program evaluation without regard to the provision in subsection 2(a)(2) of said Act of July 26, 1954, as amended, and $13,550,000 shall be available for research and special project activities under section 4(c) of said Vocational Education Act of 1963.

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that sets aside money for education research, surveys, training and demonstrations. It does not require or recommend comment periods, hearings, advisory bodies with outside members, consultation with states or others, or a right to sue. The cross-reference to subsection 2(a)(2) waives an earlier requirement for part of the funds rather than creating any outside-party process, so it does not count as participation.
opus.s: $90,967,000 of which $1,250,000 shall be available for program evaluation without regard to the provision in subsection 2(a)(2) of said Act of July 26, 1954, as amended
opus.b: This section is not participation. The tempting reading is that "without regard to the provision in subsection 2(a)(2)" brings in a procedure from the 1954 Act, possibly review by an outside panel. But that clause sets the procedure aside for the $1,250,000 evaluation money rather than requiring it, and the text never names any outside party.
